newsitem.title: FRANCE: French back government's Europe stance - poll.
newsitem.headline: French back government's Europe stance - poll.

text.p: A majority of French people think the new Socialist-led government should continue talks with its European partners to find new conditions for joining a single currency rather than doing everything possible to hit the Maastricht treaty criteria, according to a CSA poll.

Fifty-eight percent of 1,000 French people polled on June 9 said they believed France should continue talks, rather than impose new austerity to hit the strict three percent deficit target, even if this risked compromising the move to a single European currency.
Twenty-seven percent of those polled said France should do everything possible to hit the three percent target for public deficits as a percentage of gross domestic product in 1997.
The Socialist party said during its campaign before coming to power in a parliamentary election on June 1 that it wanted less dogmatic reading of the Maastricht treaty.
It said on Monday it needed time to reflect on a related EU budget stability pact and wanted talks on promoting growth and employment alongside deficit control.

According to the CSA poll, a majority of French people said the new Socialist government should continue with the previous centre-right government's plans to partially privatise France Telecom to make it more flexible in the face of international competition.

Fifty-one percent of those polled said the new government should go ahead, while 35 percent said it should abandon the project to preserve an element of public service in the telecommunications sector.
According to the poll the French would prefer partial privatisations of bank Credit Lyonnais , Thomson and Air France to total privatisations.
